summary.design: Retrospective analysis of a U.S. cardiac arrest registry from 2013 to 2023, using 70% of data to develop risk scores and 30% for internal validation; logistic regression and classification trees were compared.
summary.key_findings: Among 26,895 pediatric patients, 27.8% survived to admission and 11.9% to discharge. Separate scores were made for infants, preschool/school-age children, and adolescents. summary.bottom_line: Pediatric OHCA survival can be stratified into three meaningful risk categories using a small set of easily identified prehospital variables, with tree-based models offering simpler use and similar accuracy.

papers.ed_link: ED resuscitation of children with septic shock

clinical.rationale: This exploratory systematic review does not establish a mortality benefit or equivalence among resuscitation strategies, so it mainly informs future research rather than changing current PED practice.

research.rationale: A registered systematic review with risk-of-bias and GRADE assessment, but the exploratory meta-analysis is limited by small studies and heterogeneous interventions.

papers.one_line: An exploratory meta-analysis of pediatric septic shock resuscitation found no mortality difference between strategies, though measurement-informed resuscitation reduced 24-hour fluids.

summary.why_it_matters: Pediatric septic shock resuscitation needs to balance tissue perfusion with avoiding excess fluid, and this review highlights that different resuscitation approaches exist with unclear overall benefit.
summary.design: Prospectively registered systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of comparative studies in pediatric septic shock.
summary.key_findings: Six studies including 422 children were analyzed. Mortality was not statistically different between randomized strategies (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.60-1.28; very low certainty). Measurement-informed strategies showed a mortality RR of 0.77 (95% CI 0.46-1.27). Two small trials found lower 24-hour fluid intake with measurement-informed care (mean difference -11.47 mL/kg, 95% CI -16.88 to -6.05; moderate certainty). Acute kidney injury results were very uncertain (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.15-1.57). Other outcomes could not be pooled statistically.
summary.bottom_line: Current evidence does not prove that any specific strategy improves survival or other patient-centered outcomes, though measurement-informed resuscitation may reduce early fluid administration. Further trials linking physiological measurements or treatment rules to standard outcomes are needed.

papers.methods_note: Systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of randomized and nonrandomized comparative studies.
